question: Is the 7B timeout tail (3 of 20 rows > timeout_s=30) a property of the rows, of run position, or of neither?
answer: Neither — it is not reproducible. Two subsequent runs of the same 20 rows (one reversed, one in the identical original order) show zero rows over timeout_s and a max of 13.81 s / 14.10 s against the original 38.20 s.
why_it_was_suspected: The 3 slowest rows occupied run positions 18, 19, 20 consecutively (p = 1/C(20,3) = 0.00088 under a random arrangement), and the 3B probe — same rows, same order — showed no tail at all.

conclusion.context_prefill_note: corr(context_chars, latency) RISES to +0.800 / +0.825 once the positional artifact is gone, so prefill genuinely dominates 7B latency — but its dynamic range (6.4 s to 14.1 s) never approaches timeout_s = 30. A context bound is a mean-latency lever, NOT a timeout fix, and nothing blocks 7B on latency grounds.
